original_value: Prior normalization methods rely on affine transformations to produce arbitrary image style transfers, of which the parameters are computed in a pre-defined way. Such manually-defined nature eventually results in the high-cost and shared encoders for both style and content encoding, making style transfer systems cumbersome to be deployed in resource-constrained environments like on the mobile-terminal side. In this paper, we propose a new and generalized normalization module, termed as Dynamic Instance Normalization (DIN), that allows for flexible and more efficient arbitrary style transfers. Comprising an instance normalization and a dynamic convolution, DIN encodes a style image into learnable convolution parameters, upon which the content image is stylized. Unlike conventional methods that use shared complex encoders to encode content and style, the proposed DIN introduces a sophisticated style encoder, yet comes with a compact and lightweight content encoder for fast inference. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach yields very encouraging results on challenging style patterns and, to our best knowledge, for the first time enables an arbitrary style transfer using MobileNet-based lightweight architecture, leading to a reduction factor of more than twenty in computational cost as compared to existing approaches. Furthermore, the proposed DIN provides flexible support for state-of-the-art convolutional operations, and thus triggers novel functionalities, such as uniform-stroke placement for non-natural images and automatic spatial-stroke control.

result.paraphrase: Prior normalization approaches depend on affine transforms to achieve arbitrary image style transfer, with parameters obtained in a predefined manner. This manual design ultimately leads to high cost and shared encoders for both style and content encoding, making style transfer systems difficult to deploy in resource-limited settings such as mobile devices. In this paper, we propose a new generalized normalization module, Dynamic Instance Normalization (DIN), for more flexible and efficient arbitrary style transfer. DIN combines instance normalization with dynamic convolution, encoding a style image into learnable convolution parameters that are then used to stylize the content image. Unlike conventional methods that rely on shared, complex encoders for both content and style, the proposed DIN uses a sophisticated style encoder together with a compact, lightweight content encoder for fast inference. Experimental results show encouraging performance on difficult style patterns and, to our knowledge, for the first time enable arbitrary style transfer with a MobileNet-based lightweight architecture, reducing computational cost by more than twenty times compared with existing methods. In addition, DIN flexibly supports state-of-the-art convolution operations, enabling new functions such as uniform-stroke placement for non-natural images and automatic spatial-stroke control.
